name: Quokka
description: Quokka: a new contender for the straight land track.
biology: Brown wallaby with round ears, short broad muzzle, black nose, hunched back, cream belly, two small forearms, two strong hind legs, relatively short slender bare tail; not a squirrel tail. Racing attributes are rounded model presets with separate evidence notes.

name: Common wombat
description: Common wombat: a new contender for the straight land track.
biology: Stocky grey-brown burrowing marsupial, broad blunt bare nose, small round ears, four short strong clawed legs, almost invisible tail; adult barrel body. Racing attributes are rounded model presets with separate evidence notes.

name: Temminck's pangolin
description: Temminck's pangolin: a new contender for the straight land track.
biology: Overlapping ochre-brown keratin scales, long thick tapering scaled tail, small tapered head, no teeth visible, four limbs with large curved foreclaws, walking low; no armadillo armor bands. Racing attributes are rounded model presets with separate evidence notes.

name: Aardvark
description: Aardvark: a new contender for the straight land track.
biology: Pink-grey sparse-haired body, very long rabbit-like ears, elongated pig-like snout, arched back, four digging legs, thick tapering tail; no tusks. Racing attributes are rounded model presets with separate evidence notes.

name: Short-beaked echidna
description: Short-beaked echidna: a new contender for the straight land track.
biology: Low dark brown body covered in cream-tipped spines, long narrow tubular beak, no external ear pinnae, four short sprawling digging limbs; no porcupine tail. Racing attributes are rounded model presets with separate evidence notes.

name: Nine-banded armadillo
description: Nine-banded armadillo: a new contender for the straight land track.
biology: Grey bony armor with flexible transverse midbody bands, pointed snout, large upright ears, long ring-armored tail, four short clawed legs. Racing attributes are rounded model presets with separate evidence notes.

name: Giant anteater
description: Giant anteater: a new contender for the straight land track.
biology: Long narrow tubular muzzle, small ears, grey-brown body with bold diagonal black and white shoulder stripe, huge shaggy tail, four legs; forefeet folded onto knuckles around long claws. Racing attributes are rounded model presets with separate evidence notes.

name: Meerkat
description: Meerkat: a new contender for the straight land track.
biology: Slender sandy mongoose with dark eye patches, tiny round ears, pointed nose, faint dark back bands, thin black-tipped tail, four legs in walking stance; not upright human posture. Racing attributes are rounded model presets with separate evidence notes.

name: European badger
description: European badger: a new contender for the straight land track.
biology: Low broad grey body, white head with two bold black eye-to-ear stripes, small ears, black legs, four digging paws, short tail. Racing attributes are rounded model presets with separate evidence notes.

name: Wolverine
description: Wolverine: a new contender for the straight land track.
biology: Stocky dark brown mustelid, broad head, small rounded ears, pale tan lateral flank bands, bushy short tail and four powerful plantigrade paws; no bear hump. Racing attributes are rounded model presets with separate evidence notes.

name: Raccoon
description: Raccoon: a new contender for the straight land track.
biology: Grey coat, black eye mask, white brows and muzzle, bushy tail with distinct dark rings, four legs with dexterous five-toed forepaws. Racing attributes are rounded model presets with separate evidence notes.

name: Red panda
description: Red panda: a new contender for the straight land track.
biology: Russet fluffy coat, white ear rims and cheeks, dark tear marks, black belly and legs, long alternating russet-ringed bushy tail, four paws; not a giant panda. Racing attributes are rounded model presets with separate evidence notes.

name: Fossa
description: Fossa: a new contender for the straight land track.
biology: Long sleek tawny-brown Malagasy carnivoran, small rounded ears, catlike short muzzle, four muscular legs, very long smooth cylindrical tail; no spots. Racing attributes are rounded model presets with separate evidence notes.

name: Ring-tailed lemur
description: Ring-tailed lemur: a new contender for the straight land track.
biology: Grey lemur with white face, black eye patches and muzzle, orange eyes, very long black-and-white ringed tail arcing behind, four limbs in terrestrial walk; no extra tail. Racing attributes are rounded model presets with separate evidence notes.

name: Olive baboon
description: Olive baboon: a new contender for the straight land track.
biology: Adult olive-brown baboon with long dark dog-like muzzle, small rounded ears, four strong limbs in quadrupedal walk, single arched tail with downturned end; not a tailless ape. Racing attributes are rounded model presets with separate evidence notes.

name: Crested porcupine
description: Crested porcupine: a new contender for the straight land track.
biology: Large dark rodent, long black-and-white banded quills fanning backwards and tall head crest, small rounded ears, blunt muzzle, four short clawed legs, short quilled tail. Racing attributes are rounded model presets with separate evidence notes.

name: European hedgehog
description: European hedgehog: a new contender for the straight land track.
biology: Small domed brown spine-covered body, pale furry pointed face, tiny round ears, black nose, four short feet; not porcupine-long quills. Racing attributes are rounded model presets with separate evidence notes.

name: Tailless tenrec
description: Tailless tenrec: a new contender for the straight land track.
biology: Coarse brown bristly body with sparse short spines, long pointed pale muzzle, prominent whiskers, small ears, four short legs, no conspicuous tail; not a hedgehog ball. Racing attributes are rounded model presets with separate evidence notes.

name: Common shrew
description: Common shrew: a new contender for the straight land track.
biology: Tiny dark brown velvety mammal, elongated flexible pointed snout, tiny eyes and ears, pale belly, four small feet, slender medium-length tail; not a mouse with round ears. Racing attributes are rounded model presets with separate evidence notes.

name: Black and rufous sengi
description: Black and rufous sengi: a new contender for the straight land track.
biology: Rufous forebody and black hindquarters, long flexible downward-pointed trunk-like snout, large ears, slender long legs, narrow bare tail; not a miniature elephant. Racing attributes are rounded model presets with separate evidence notes.

name: South African springhare
description: South African springhare: a new contender for the straight land track.
biology: Sandy large jumping rodent, long ears, large dark eyes, two short forelimbs and two extremely long hind feet, long furry black-tipped tail, cream belly; not a kangaroo pouch. Racing attributes are rounded model presets with separate evidence notes.

name: Okapi
description: Okapi: a new contender for the straight land track.
biology: Dark chocolate adult forest giraffid, short neck, large rounded ears, white lower face, white zebra-like stripes only on rump and upper legs, four long cloven-hoofed legs, small ossicones; not a full striped zebra. Racing attributes are rounded model presets with separate evidence notes.

name: Southern cassowary
description: Southern cassowary: a new contender for the straight land track.
biology: Adult black shaggy flightless bird, bare cobalt-blue neck, two red wattles, tall brown casque on head, two powerful grey three-toed legs with long inner claws, tiny folded wings. Racing attributes are rounded model presets with separate evidence notes.

name: Emu
description: Emu: a new contender for the straight land track.
biology: Tall flightless bird with shaggy brown drooping double feathers, dark head and blue-grey upper neck, short broad beak, two long strong grey three-toed legs, tiny near-invisible wings; no casque. Racing attributes are rounded model presets with separate evidence notes.

name: Secretary bird
description: Secretary bird: a new contender for the straight land track.
biology: Tall grey terrestrial raptor, long black-feathered thighs and long bare lower legs, black quill crest behind head, orange-red bare eye patch, hooked beak, long central tail feathers and two folded wings. Racing attributes are rounded model presets with separate evidence notes.

name: Greater roadrunner
description: Greater roadrunner: a new contender for the straight land track.
biology: Slender streaked brown ground cuckoo, erect ragged crest, long straight tail, pointed grey beak, pale belly, two long running legs with two toes forward and two back; no cartoon purple plumage. Racing attributes are rounded model presets with separate evidence notes.

name: North Island brown kiwi
description: North Island brown kiwi: a new contender for the straight land track.
biology: Round brown shaggy flightless bird, very long slender ivory bill with nostrils at tip, tiny eyes, no visible tail, wings hidden in plumage, two sturdy three-toed legs. Racing attributes are rounded model presets with separate evidence notes.

name: Wild turkey
description: Wild turkey: a new contender for the straight land track.
biology: Adult male dark bronze wild turkey, bare blue-red head and red wattle, modest snood, folded wings, closed broad brown barred tail rather than display fan, two sturdy scaly legs. Racing attributes are rounded model presets with separate evidence notes.

name: Helmeted guineafowl
description: Helmeted guineafowl: a new contender for the straight land track.
biology: Round charcoal body densely patterned with small white spots, tiny blue bare head with brown helmet and red wattles, short tail, folded wings, two dark running legs. Racing attributes are rounded model presets with separate evidence notes.

name: Indian peafowl
description: Indian peafowl: a new contender for the straight land track.
biology: Adult male with blue neck and head, small upright fan crest, green scaled upper back, long folded green eye-spotted train trailing compactly behind, two legs and folded wings; full train in frame, no display fan. Racing attributes are rounded model presets with separate evidence notes.

name: Red-legged seriema
description: Red-legged seriema: a new contender for the straight land track.
biology: Long-legged buff-grey ground bird, red bill and legs, upright wispy forehead crest, long neck, dark barred tail, folded wings; two three-forward-toed feet, not a secretary bird. Racing attributes are rounded model presets with separate evidence notes.

name: Kori bustard
description: Kori bustard: a new contender for the straight land track.
biology: Large heavy brown mottled ground bird, thick grey barred neck, black swept-back crown tuft, white belly, long pale legs, folded wings and short tail; two three-toed feet. Racing attributes are rounded model presets with separate evidence notes.

name: Great tinamou
description: Great tinamou: a new contender for the straight land track.
biology: Plump olive-brown subtly barred forest bird, small grey head and slender neck, short slightly curved bill, very short tail, tucked wings, two stout grey legs; not a kiwi beak. Racing attributes are rounded model presets with separate evidence notes.

name: Superb lyrebird
description: Superb lyrebird: a new contender for the straight land track.
biology: Brown adult male ground bird, long delicate tail with two outer lyre-shaped feathers and fine central filaments, slim dark beak, strong scratching feet, two folded wings; tail arched compactly fully in frame. Racing attributes are rounded model presets with separate evidence notes.

name: Komodo dragon
description: Komodo dragon: a new contender for the straight land track.
biology: Heavy grey-brown monitor lizard with granular scales, long low head, four powerful splayed clawed limbs, very long muscular tapering tail, forked tongue; no spikes, frill or wings. Racing attributes are rounded model presets with separate evidence notes.

name: Gila monster
description: Gila monster: a new contender for the straight land track.
biology: Stocky orange-pink and black bead-scaled lizard, broad head, thick short banded tail, four short splayed clawed limbs; no dorsal spines. Racing attributes are rounded model presets with separate evidence notes.

name: Central bearded dragon
description: Central bearded dragon: a new contender for the straight land track.
biology: Sandy tan lizard with broad triangular head, spiny beard under jaw, flattened oval body, small lateral spines, four splayed clawed legs, long tapering tail; no neck frill. Racing attributes are rounded model presets with separate evidence notes.

name: Frilled lizard
description: Frilled lizard: a new contender for the straight land track.
biology: Brown slender lizard with large circular pleated orange-edged neck frill partly expanded, two long hind legs in bipedal run and two small raised forelegs, very long thin tail; no extra legs. Racing attributes are rounded model presets with separate evidence notes.

name: Texas horned lizard
description: Texas horned lizard: a new contender for the straight land track.
biology: Broad flattened sand-coloured body, crown of pointed head horns, two long rear head horns, rough spiny back and side fringes, four short splayed legs, short pointed tail; not thorny devil. Racing attributes are rounded model presets with separate evidence notes.

name: Thorny devil
description: Thorny devil: a new contender for the straight land track.
biology: Ochre and brown desert lizard densely covered in large conical spines, hornlike head spikes, false-head hump behind neck, four short splayed limbs, stiff short spiny tail. Racing attributes are rounded model presets with separate evidence notes.

name: Eastern blue-tongued skink
description: Eastern blue-tongued skink: a new contender for the straight land track.
biology: Smooth shiny broad brown-banded skink, large triangular head, briefly visible broad blue tongue, cylindrical body, four very small five-toed legs, thick tapering tail. Racing attributes are rounded model presets with separate evidence notes.

name: Leopard gecko
description: Leopard gecko: a new contender for the straight land track.
biology: Yellow and pale cream gecko with black spots, moveable eyelids, thick segmented fat tail, four small legs with clawed slender toes WITHOUT adhesive toe pads. Racing attributes are rounded model presets with separate evidence notes.

name: Tuatara
description: Tuatara: a new contender for the straight land track.
biology: Stout olive-grey reptile, triangular head, small white dorsal crest from head along back, four sprawling clawed limbs, long thick tapering tail; modest crest, no iguana dewlap. Racing attributes are rounded model presets with separate evidence notes.

name: Rosy boa
description: Rosy boa: a new contender for the straight land track.
biology: Small thick-bodied smooth-scaled boa, three reddish-brown LONGITUDINAL stripes on pale cream-grey body, blunt small head, compact flowing S-shaped slither right; absolutely no limbs, no hood. Racing attributes are rounded model presets with separate evidence notes.

name: Common toad
description: Common toad: a new contender for the straight land track.
biology: Warty brown adult toad, squat body, copper eyes with horizontal pupils, large oval parotoid glands behind eyes, two short forelegs and two bent hind legs, no tail. Racing attributes are rounded model presets with separate evidence notes.

name: Fire salamander
description: Fire salamander: a new contender for the straight land track.
biology: Shiny black terrestrial salamander with irregular bold yellow patches, broad head, four short limbs, four front toes and five rear toes, round-section tapering tail; no gills or fins. Racing attributes are rounded model presets with separate evidence notes.

name: Tiger salamander
description: Tiger salamander: a new contender for the straight land track.
biology: Stout terrestrial adult salamander, dark brown body with irregular yellow-olive blotches, broad round head, four short limbs, long thick tapering tail; no external larval gills. Racing attributes are rounded model presets with separate evidence notes.

name: Tomato frog
description: Tomato frog: a new contender for the straight land track.
biology: Round plump red-orange adult female terrestrial frog, orange eyes, pale belly, two small forelegs and two short folded hind legs, no horns, no tail. Racing attributes are rounded model presets with separate evidence notes.

name: Ornate horned frog
description: Ornate horned frog: a new contender for the straight land track.
biology: Broad round green and brown patterned terrestrial frog, enormous wide mouth, small pointed raised eyelid horns, pale underside, two small forelegs and two folded powerful hind legs; not bull horns. Racing attributes are rounded model presets with separate evidence notes.

name: Golden mantella
description: Golden mantella: a new contender for the straight land track.
biology: Tiny uniformly bright golden-orange terrestrial frog, without dark dorsal spots, black round eyes, smooth skin, two small forelegs and two folded long hind legs, slender toes, no tail; no oversized treefrog toe discs. Racing attributes are rounded model presets with separate evidence notes.

name: Chilean rose tarantula
description: Chilean rose tarantula: a new contender for the straight land track.
biology: Hairy brown tarantula with pinkish copper carapace, TWO body sections, EIGHT jointed walking legs, two short pedipalps beside downward fangs, tiny clustered real spider eyes; no antennae, no cartoon eyeball stalks. Racing attributes are rounded model presets with separate evidence notes.

name: Emperor scorpion
description: Emperor scorpion: a new contender for the straight land track.
biology: Glossy black scorpion, EIGHT walking legs plus TWO large grasping pedipalp pincers, segmented narrow tail curving above back ending in reddish stinger, small eyes; no antennae. Racing attributes are rounded model presets with separate evidence notes.

name: Coconut crab
description: Coconut crab: a new contender for the straight land track.
biology: Adult terrestrial coconut crab, blue-purple and rust armored broad body, two massive front claws with left larger, three pairs of obvious walking legs, reduced rear fifth pair tucked under body, long antennae, short abdomen curled under, no external shell. Racing attributes are rounded model presets with separate evidence notes.

name: Six-spotted tiger beetle
description: Six-spotted tiger beetle: a new contender for the straight land track.
biology: Metallic emerald green beetle, six small cream elytral spots, large eyes and curved jaws, SIX long jointed running legs, two antennae, closed wing cases; never eight legs. Racing attributes are rounded model presets with separate evidence notes.

name: Saharan silver ant
description: Saharan silver ant: a new contender for the straight land track.
biology: Silvery-haired desert worker ant, three clear body regions, narrow waist, SIX long thin jointed legs, two elbowed antennae, large dark eyes, no wings. Racing attributes are rounded model presets with separate evidence notes.

name: Madagascar hissing cockroach
description: Madagascar hissing cockroach: a new contender for the straight land track.
biology: Large wingless mahogany and black oval cockroach, segmented abdomen, broad dark shield behind small head, two long antennae, SIX spiny running legs, no wings. Racing attributes are rounded model presets with separate evidence notes.

name: European mantis
description: European mantis: a new contender for the straight land track.
biology: Adult green praying mantis, triangular mobile head, two compound eyes, two fine antennae, long prothorax, SIX legs total: two folded spined raptorial forelegs and four walking legs, folded wings. Racing attributes are rounded model presets with separate evidence notes.

name: Indian stick insect
description: Indian stick insect: a new contender for the straight land track.
biology: Wingless brown-green stick insect, extremely elongated twiglike body, SIX very long slender jointed legs, two fine antennae, tiny head, no leaf wings. Racing attributes are rounded model presets with separate evidence notes.

name: Giant African millipede
description: Giant African millipede: a new contender for the straight land track.
biology: Glossy dark chocolate cylindrical millipede with many ring segments, TWO PAIRS of short reddish legs per midbody segment, two short antennae, compact shallow C-shaped right-facing walking form; no pincers. Racing attributes are rounded model presets with separate evidence notes.

name: Giant desert centipede
description: Giant desert centipede: a new contender for the straight land track.
biology: Flattened reddish-brown centipede with dark head, 21 pairs of yellow legs, ONE leg pair per trunk segment, long antennae, elongated rear leg pair; no millipede cylinder, no scorpion tail. Racing attributes are rounded model presets with separate evidence notes.

name: Common earthworm
description: Common earthworm: a new contender for the straight land track.
biology: Pink-brown segmented adult earthworm with swollen pale clitellum nearer front, tapering ends, compact natural curve facing right, NO eyes, NO limbs, NO antennae; subtle moist shading without slime trail. Racing attributes are rounded model presets with separate evidence notes.

name: Black slug
description: Black slug: a new contender for the straight land track.
biology: Black terrestrial slug, rounded mantle on front back, elongated muscular foot, TWO upper eye-bearing tentacles and TWO short lower sensory tentacles, no shell, no limbs, no trail. Racing attributes are rounded model presets with separate evidence notes.

name: Solórzano's velvet worm
description: Giant velvet worm: a new contender for the straight land track.
biology: Brown velvety soft wormlike body, 34 pairs of short closely spaced unjointed stubby lobopod legs in an adult male, two curved antennae, tiny dark eyes and two small oral papillae; no insect armor or centipede joints. Racing attributes are rounded model presets with separate evidence notes.

name: Common rough woodlouse
description: Common rough woodlouse: a new contender for the straight land track.
biology: Small grey flattened oval terrestrial isopod, rough overlapping dorsal plates, SEVEN pairs of walking legs, two main antennae, short rear uropods, no snail shell, walking rather than rolled up. Racing attributes are rounded model presets with separate evidence notes.
